wrong_text: it is screened for nine rare but serious conditions
problem: The NHS newborn blood spot programme screened for 9 conditions until September 2025, when hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1 (HT1) was added as the 10th condition. The NHS webpage (last reviewed 5 Sep 2024, updated with HT1 from Oct 2025) now states 10 conditions. All references to '9' in this lesson are out of date. Source: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/baby/newborn-screening/blood-spot-test/ and https://www.england.nhs.uk/2025/10/nhs-to-screen-all-newborn-babies-for-life-threatening-metabolic-disorder/
correction: Replace '9' / 'nine' with '10' / 'ten' throughout. Add hereditary tyrosinaemia type 1 (HT1) to the list of screened conditions alongside the existing 9. Affected locations: n7 paragraph ('nine rare but serious conditions'), Key Fact box ('screens for nine conditions'), conclusion bullet, practice question mark scheme, KC option ('Nine conditions'), flashcard answer ('Nine conditions').

wrong_text: At 12 weeks: 6-in-1 vaccine (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, Hib, hepatitis B), Rotavirus (second dose), PCV (pneumococcal). At 16 weeks: 6-in-1 (third dose), MenB (second dose).
problem: The MenB second dose moved from 16 weeks to 12 weeks from 1 July 2025. The PCV first dose moved from 12 weeks to 16 weeks at the same time to free the appointment slot. The current schedule (effective July 2025, confirmed in the Jan 2026 updated schedule at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-complete-routine-immunisation-schedule/complete-routine-immunisation-schedule-from-1-january-2026) is: 12 weeks = 6-in-1 (2nd dose) + MenB (2nd dose) + Rotavirus (2nd dose); 16 weeks = 6-in-1 (3rd dose) + PCV (1st dose). The lesson has MenB and PCV at the wrong ages.
correction: At 12 weeks: 6-in-1 vaccine (second dose), MenB (second dose), Rotavirus (second dose). At 16 weeks: 6-in-1 (third dose), PCV (pneumococcal — first dose).

wrong_text: At 1 year (12–13 months): Hib/MenC booster, MMR (measles, mumps, rubella), PCV booster, MenB booster.
problem: Three errors in this line. (1) The Hib/MenC booster has been discontinued for children born on or after 1 July 2024 — the sole brand (Menitorix) is no longer manufactured. (2) MMR has been replaced by MMRV (measles, mumps, rubella and varicella/chickenpox) from 1 January 2026 for children born on/after 1 July 2024. (3) The PCV booster is still given at 1 year, which is correct, but the overall line is substantially wrong. Source: https://ukhsa.blog.gov.uk/2025/12/30/changes-to-the-childhood-vaccination-schedule-from-january-2026/
correction: At 1 year (12–13 months): MMRV vaccine (measles, mumps, rubella and varicella — first dose), PCV booster, MenB booster. Note: the Hib/MenC booster has been discontinued for children born from July 2024 onwards.

wrong_text: At 3 years 4 months: 4-in-1 pre-school booster (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio), MMR second dose.
problem: From January 2026, children born on or after 1 July 2024 receive their second dose of the measles-containing vaccine (now MMRV) at a new 18-month appointment, not at 3 years 4 months. The 3-year-4-month appointment retains the 4-in-1 pre-school booster (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio), but the MMR/MMRV second dose has moved earlier. Children born before 1 July 2024 do still receive the second MMR at 3y4m under the transitional arrangement. The lesson presents the old schedule only. Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-complete-routine-immunisation-schedule/complete-routine-immunisation-schedule-from-1-january-2026
correction: At 18 months (new appointment, children born on/after 1 July 2024): 6-in-1 (fourth dose), MMRV second dose. At 3 years 4 months: 4-in-1 pre-school booster (diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio). Note for the lesson: the MMR second dose has moved from 3 years 4 months to 18 months for children born from July 2024 — the schedule was updated in January 2026. Also update flashcard 'At what age is the MMR vaccine first given in the UK? ... with a second dose at 3 years 4 months' to reflect the new 18-month second dose for children born from July 2024.

wrong_text: At 2–3 years annually: Flu vaccine (nasal spray).
problem: Minor imprecision: the annual children's flu nasal spray is offered from 2 years through to (and including) Year 11 at school (approximately age 16), not just 2–3 years. However, the schedule text is specifically listing the 'routine childhood' points; this item is correct in stating 2–3 years as an example entry point. This is a low-severity imprecision rather than a factual error — consider clarifying 'from 2 years old each autumn' to avoid implying it stops at age 3.
correction: At 2 years and annually each autumn: Flu vaccine (nasal spray). (The programme continues through primary and secondary school age, offered annually.)
